To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ca2+ is accumulated in mitochondria of intact neurons and that this Ca2+ is released from mitochondria under the effect of uncouplers of oxidative phosphorylation.

the protonophore FCCP stimulates Ca2+ release from glutamate-loaded cerebellar granular cell mitochondria, and that this release can be inhibited by the mitochondrial Ca2+-binding protein cyclosporin A.

the protonophore FCCP induced Ca2+ efflux from mitochondria of intact neurons in a Ca2+-free medium, that the effect of FCCP on Ca2+ release was inhibited by cyclosporin A, and that oligomycin, a blocker of ATP-synthase, prevented the glutamate-induced decrease of intracellar ATP level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of Ca2+ release from mitochondria in glutamate-treated neurons and its dependence on ATP-synthase activity.
the study of Ca2+ homeostasis in mitochondria of cerebellar neurons and the role of the Ca2+ uniporter in this process.
the study of mitochondrial Ca2+ transport in intact neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mitochondrial Ca2+ accumulation and storage are regulated by the energy status of the cell.
the cyclosporin A-sensitive pore is formed in mitochondria of intact neurons under the effect glutamate-induced increase in Ca2+ level and uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation.

Ca2+ is stored for a long time in mitochondria of intact neurons and that this Ca2+ is released by a cyclosporin-sensitive mechanism, probably through a Ca2+ channel in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mitochondrial pore induced by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation is a sensitive target for cyclosporin A, and this effect of cyclosporin may be one of the mechanisms of its neuroprotective activity.
in glutamate-treated cells, a cyclosporin A-sensitive Ca2+ channel in the mitochondrial inner membrane is induced and this channel is activated during uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation.

in neurons Ca2+ accumulated in mitochondria under the effect of uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation is released from mitochondria in response to the decrease of the membrane potential and that this release is mediated by the cyclosporin A-sensitive pore.
The main takeaway from our work is that
uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation in intact mitochondria of neurons can lead to the induction of cyclosporin A-sensitive pore.
uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation by protonophore FCCP in glutamate-loaded neurons results in Ca2+ release from mitochondria via the formation of a cyclosporin A-sensitive pore.
in neurons, as in other cells, the cyclosporin A-sensitive Ca2+ pore can be induced during uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation.
